notable.headline: WD-40 Q4 EPS $1.06 misses $1.15; sales $176.8M beat $172.1M; sees FY27 adj EPS $6.40-$6.70 vs $6.48 est, sales $715M-$735M vs $727.3M est
notable.read: Mixed print reported after the close on 10-21: EPS miss on margins, revenue beat. FY27 EPS guidance midpoint ($6.55) is slightly above consensus, but the sales midpoint ($725M) is slightly below. Resolves the high-risk flag from 10-20/21 with a mixed result; watch the reaction.

notable.headline: Stifel lowers PT to $537; Deutsche Bank $561 (from $559); Goldman $573 (from $564); Morgan Stanley $480 (from $470)
notable.read: Continues the 10-21 story (Q3 double miss, guidance affirmed, leveraged-debt slowdown). Sell-side reaction is split rather than a rush to cut: ratings are holding at Buy and most PT changes are small, with Stifel the one cut. That makes it a softer reaction than the miss alone suggested.

notable.headline: Cheniere units sign LNG SPAs with QatarEnergy for 4 MTPA through 2054
notable.read: Large, long-dated offtake agreement (no 8-K 1.01 in the input yet; a filing may follow). Positive for the contract book and visibility ahead of 10-29 earnings, though a state-backed supplier signing at Cheniere also reflects strong LNG demand amid Middle East disruption. Material-deal category, so worth a line.

notable.headline: Affirm exclusive BNPL deal with Sam's Club; Walmart launches Agent Gateway and Agent Profiles for third-party AI shopping agents
notable.read: Continues the constructive 10-20 sentiment (Deutsche upgrade, Evercore $130, membership bundle). The Affirm deal is a modest revenue and financing partnership; the agent gateway is a strategic positioning move on agentic commerce, with profiles launching next month. Neither is material near term. Earnings are 11-19, far off.

notable.headline: Australian court orders alternative app distribution and payments from 2027-03-01 (rejects Epic's global relief); iPhone Duo launches 10-23 with limited walk-in units; Omdia: global smartphone shipments down 20% y/y in 3Q
notable.read: The court ruling adds to the incremental regulatory pressure (UK CMA, Poland) but is contained to Australia and a distant date. The Omdia market-contraction number is a demand warning for the category, offset by Apple's 22% share and the Duo supply tightness. Net: another cautious data point going into the 10-28 event and the uncertain earnings date (10-29 vs 11-02).
